title: The Property Set on Nothing: A Misspelt Name, a Binding That Was Assigned Over, and a Probe That Says So

questions.question: QObject::setProperty("widht", 300) is called on an item whose property is width. What happens?
options: It returns false, creates a dynamic property named widht, and the width is unchanged

questions.question: property("nothingLikeThis") is converted to a double. What is it?
options: 0, from an invalid QVariant: nothing says the name was wrong
questions.explanation: It was invalid and converted to 0.

questions.question: A bound width is assigned in JavaScript, and then its source changes. What does the width do?
options: Stays: the assignment replaced the binding
questions.explanation: After width = 10 and outer 400, inner was 10.

questions.question: How is the binding put back?
options: Assign Qt.binding(function) so that it follows again
questions.explanation: After Qt.binding and outer 500, inner was 250.

questions.question: What does evaluate return for an undefined name?
options: ok false with the message ReferenceError: ... is not defined
ok true and an empty value
questions.explanation: None of the failures was ok, and none threw.

questions.question: Why does the probe write through QQmlProperty and not setProperty?
options: QQmlProperty knows what the object declares, and says so when a name is not one
questions.explanation: A name that is not a property is an error and creates nothing.
